message:
As Enclosure and Structural Designer, the box that holds 1 tonne is a small walk-in that a person can stand in and that keeps the leak inside the refrigeration budget, Cold-Chain Refrigeration Engineer.

In plain words thick foam gives a low leak so the harvest heat dominates, and published sandwich-panel tables set the thickness. The table in Professional Manufacturer Factory Keep Warm Insulated PU Sandwich Panel (E32) gives U Value PIR 0.21 watt per square metre kelvin at 100 millimetre and 0.17 watt per square metre kelvin at 120 millimetre, and the comparison in Sandwich Panel Types: PU, PIR, EPS & Rock Wool Compared (E33) states 100 millimetre Polyurethane (PU, foam insulation) reaches about 0.23 watt per square metre kelvin, so I use Polyisocyanurate (PIR, rigid foam insulation) 100 millimetre walls and 120 millimetre roof and floor at about 0.21 watt per square metre kelvin. The precedent in Cold Storage Room (E34) lists a 1 Metric Tonne Vegetable Cold Storage Room at Dimension 4 metre by 4 metre by 3 metre, while my smaller interior 2.4 metre by 1.8 metre by 2.0 metre high gives interior volume 8.64 cubic metres in the interior volume estimate (E39), envelope area 25.4 square metres in the envelope area estimate (E40), and conduction 203 watt at 43 degree Celsius ambient minus 5 degree Celsius room in the conduction estimate (E41), about a small bedroom in everyday scale and inside your 350 watt steady assumption in the revised steady-load simulation (E28).

In plain words the produce sits in standard vented vegetable boxes on open steel shelves with air gaps for your rear-to-front air, Manager. The listing in Best Folding Vented 600x400 Plastic Crates for Sale (E36) gives Footprint 600 by 400 millimetre, Material Food-Grade Polypropylene, and Airflow Fully Vented Walls and Base, so two slotted-angle rows carry fifty 600 millimetre by 400 millimetre crates at 20.0 kilogram each for 1000 kilogram total, hose-cleanable with removable shelves, shown with the high rear evaporator loop and low return in the walk-in chamber sketch (E42).

In plain words the whole cold box stands on farm soil without foundations and the sun panels never pull on the foam, Solar Energy Systems Engineer. Six precast pads with adjustable feet carry a raised insulated floor plinth plus a hinged insulated door with Polyvinyl Chloride (PVC, flexible plastic) strip curtain, while Photovoltaic (PV, solar electricity) modules sit on a separate galvanized tube gantry over the roof with a vent gap as sunshade in that same walk-in chamber sketch (E42), so unprepared ground sees only about a person-weight per pad and soft gaskets to rigid panels to racking carry no point loads through foam.

I am not ready because door openings per day and a bench test for 43 degree pull-down must still confirm the curtain and seal choice.
